Gap: Neither TaskItem nor CalendarEvent is registered in EntityRegistry
Evidence: BL/Platform/EntityRegistry.cs — the codes are SalesInvoice, PurchaseInvoice, Quotation, JournalEntry, Customer, Supplier, ManufWorkOrder, PosOrder, Employee, Project, Item, PlatformRoleAssignment. No Task, no CalendarEvent.
WhyItBlocksIntegration: No timeline, no comments, no files, no followers, and no other record can link TO a task. Tasks CONSUME the registry (BL/TaskLinkResolver.cs is a wrapper over IEntityRegistry) but are absent FROM it — the asymmetry is the single biggest blocker.

Gap: Neither module raises a business event
Evidence: grep for RecordAsync / IBusinessEventService across BL/Task*.cs and BL/CalendarService.cs returns nothing.
WhyItBlocksIntegration: Nothing from Tasks or Calendar reaches the outbox, so the timeline and the notification projection can never see them however well they are registered.

Gap: Tasks and Calendar are completely disconnected from each other
Evidence: TaskItem has DueDate but no calendar reference; CalendarEvent has no EntityType/EntityId and no TaskId. Neither service references the other.
WhyItBlocksIntegration: A task's due date never appears on a calendar, and an event cannot carry or create a task. This is the integration the increment exists to enable.

Gap: Tasks raise NO notifications at all
Evidence: grep NotifyAsync/NotifyRoleAsync across Controllers/TasksController.cs, BL/TaskService.cs, BL/TaskGeneratorService.cs, BL/TaskScheduleMatcher.cs — no match.
WhyItBlocksIntegration: Assignment, reassignment, due-soon, overdue, completion and auto-generation are all silent. A task assigned to you today notifies you never.

Gap: Calendar notifies only on invite, and only from the controller
Evidence: Controllers/CalendarController.cs:104 NotifyAsync on invite. BL/CalendarService.cs contains no notification at all.
WhyItBlocksIntegration: Reschedule, cancellation and reminders are silent, and the one notification that exists sits in the controller, so any non-controller caller skips it.

Gap: No time-zone model; the two modules disagree about time
Evidence: BL/CalendarService.cs writes DateTime.Now and emits ISO WITHOUT an offset (Iso() at line 129, deliberately, so FullCalendar reads it as entered). TaskItem.CreatedAt is DateTime.UtcNow while DueDate is a bare local value.
WhyItBlocksIntegration: Merging a task due date and a calendar event onto one surface will place them at different real instants for anyone not in the server's zone.

Gap: No recurrence anywhere in either module
Evidence: TaskAutoRule.RuleType is a FIXED set of five system-state rules (LowStock, OverdueInvoice, WorkOrderQc, DeliveryReady, NewEmployeeOnboard, BL/TaskGeneratorService.cs:29-33). CalendarEvent has no RRULE, no series and no exception dates.
WhyItBlocksIntegration: TM-7 is rule-driven creation and TM-9 is movement matching; NEITHER is a schedule. 'Every Sunday' cannot be expressed for a task or an event.

Gap: Calendar attendees are replaced by delete-and-reinsert on every save
WhyItBlocksIntegration: Attendee rows have no stable identity, so a response status (accepted/declined/tentative) cannot be added later without losing it on the next save. The same identity anti-pattern this tab already remediated as CR-01 in the construction track.

Gap: Calendar has no attendee response status and no organiser delegation
Evidence: Models/Context/Calendar/CalendarEvent.cs — CalendarEventAttendee carries only EventId and EmployeeId. BL/CalendarService.cs:92,122 — only the owner may edit or delete.
WhyItBlocksIntegration: An invitation cannot be accepted or declined, and an assistant cannot manage an executive's calendar.

Gap: No external calendar synchronisation of any kind
Evidence: No ICS/iCal export, no CalDAV, no Exchange/Graph or Google client anywhere in BL/.
WhyItBlocksIntegration: 'Calendar synchronization' has no existing mechanism to extend — it is new work, and its direction (one-way publish vs two-way sync) is an unmade decision.

Gap: Tasks and Calendar SQL carries almost no database integrity
Evidence: Across the 11 tasks_*.sql scripts and calendar.sql: 0 FOREIGN KEY, 0 CHECK, 0 ROWVERSION, 3 UNIQUE in total.
WhyItBlocksIntegration: Integration multiplies the cost of a bad row: a task linked to a deleted entity, or an attendee row pointing at nobody, becomes visible on the timeline and the workspace.

Gap: TasksController is largely ungated and hardcodes company 1
Evidence: Controllers/TasksController.cs:17 DefaultCompanyId = 1; only 3 references to TasksActions in the whole controller, while TasksAccessService defines 8 actions.
WhyItBlocksIntegration: A workspace that surfaces tasks across modules would widen the blast radius of an unenforced check.
Owner: FIRST TAB — referred, not fixed here

Gap: Task status is a free string with no state machine
Evidence: TaskItem.Status — New | InProgress | Done, with 'Overdue' derived. No transition table; ChangeStatusAsync validates the target value only.
WhyItBlocksIntegration: A timeline that shows 'status changed' needs to know which transitions are legal to render them meaningfully.

Gap: No task dependencies, no subtasks, no checklist
Evidence: TaskItem has no ParentId and no predecessor/successor relation.
WhyItBlocksIntegration: A workspace cannot show a blocked task, and construction's future WBS activities cannot hang scheduling off tasks.

Gap: Calendar is absent from the Workspace shell that now exists
Evidence: BL/Workspace/WorkspaceService.cs injects ITaskService (line 43) and states 'MY WORK - consumes ITaskService. No task rule is re-implemented here.' (line 164). It injects no ICalendarService and exposes no agenda panel.
WhyItBlocksIntegration: The workspace surface this increment was preparing contracts for already exists and already shows tasks. Calendar is the missing half, so 'my day' shows work but not meetings.

Gap: Calendar event has no category, colour or entity link for the workspace
Evidence: CalendarEvent carries Scope (Personal|Company) and nothing else classifiable.
WhyItBlocksIntegration: The workspace cannot filter 'show me only site inspections' without a classification.
